title: Validator and Repair Effects Under Shared-Initial-Candidate Semantics: A Paired Study of a Guarded LLM→NetOps Pipeline
abstract: We report a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measured the effect of a deterministic validator and an at-most-one repair step applied to the same sampled LLM candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics) in a guarded NetOps pipeline. The preregistered study targeted retrieval-augmentation (RAG) poisoning attacks, but the executed adapter contract disabled retrievals (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); consequently the realized estimand compares baseline single-shot validator outcomes on a shared sampled candidate against final guarded outcomes (validator ± permitted repair) on that same candidate. On N = 250 synthetic intent→configuration tasks the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 judged every sampled initial candidate valid (n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0), no repairs were applied, and baseline and guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rates were identical (1.0). Mapping actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms; paired difference = 0.0 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable in this run; we document this execution-time realization, reconcile the archived artifacts, quantify the power/assumption mismatch (preregistered baseline ≈ 0.05 vs. observed 0.0), and discuss construct, internal, and external validity limitations with artifact-grounded recommendations for follow-up preregistered experiments.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation, staged change workflows, and zero-touch automation. Unconstrained LLM outputs can violate operational invariants (ordering, reachability, policy), motivating guarded architectures that pair generation with deterministic validators and bounded repairs (generate→validate→repair). We preregistered candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1 to quantify whether targeted poisoning of retrieval contexts (RAG) increases actionable-misconfiguration rates and whether deterministic defenses reduce that effect. The executed adapter contract, however, used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and retrieval_augmented_generation = false (artifact-backed), so the empirical estimand realized by the run compares: (a) baseline single-shot validator result on a single sampled candidate versus (b) the final guarded result after any permitted repair on that same candidate. This paper (1) reports the preregistration and the executed contract, (2) presents confirmatory artifact-backed results under executed semantics, (3) documents the execution-time realization that retrievals were disabled and reconciles the archived metadata, and (4) discusses threats to validity and concrete follow-up preregistration targets. Our contribution is an artifact-grounded empirical account of guarded-pipeline behavior when baseline and guarded arms begin from exactly the same sampled candidate.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and application papers document active interest in LLM-driven NetOps, including intent decomposition, configuration generation, and zero-touch automation; they also recommend integrating deterministic verifiers and simulators as validators [cited_record_ids]. Work in adjacent domains (code translation, SOC RAG pipelines) documents concrete failure modes—translation bugs, hallucinations, and adversarially induced misinformation—that motivate tool-augmented mitigations but do not establish their generality in NetOps. Prior research has proposed and prototyped tool-augmented and verifier-assisted pipelines; these works indicate potential grounding improvements but also highlight engineering and system tradeoffs (latency, complexity) and do not provide broad, topology-grounded empirical measurements of RAG-poisoning effects on operational invariants. The present study addresses a narrowly scoped empirical question under the executed semantics: when baseline and guarded arms share a single sampled candidate, does a deterministic validator plus a bounded repair change the paired actionable-misconfiguration outcome?
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and executed contract. The study was preregistered as candidate-2026-003-prereg-v1. The preregistered manifest and execution artifacts are archived; the preregistration SHA-256 is ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3 (execution manifest). The executed adapter family was hosted_netops_gvr_v1 requesting model declared as gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses). Key executed contract fields (artifact-backed): generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across baseline and guarded arms); retrieval_augmented_generation = false (no retrievals, hence no RAG/poisoning injection); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; task_count = 250; planned_episode_count = 500; completed_episode_count = 500; model_calls_used = 250. The archived model_configuration.json path and artifact hash are execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and must not be interpreted as temperature = 0.

Estimand mapping and operationalization. The preregistration defined the primary estimand as the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate under poisoned versus clean retrievals at poison_fraction = 0.30. Because retrievals were disabled in execution, the realized estimand is different and is stated explicitly: executed estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics, where each task yields exactly one sampled candidate reused by both conditions. We operationalized VALID_CONFIGURATION (archived per-episode validator output) so that actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. The primary confirmatory test is the paired comparison of this binary indicator between baseline (validator on shared initial candidate) and guarded (final validator result after any permitted repair on the same candidate).

Run-time semantics and sampling. For each of 250 tasks the adapter executed one shared initial-generation call; provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json / execution manifest) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 250 and stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 250}. Exactly one shared_initial_candidate per task was recorded and reused by both arms; there were no independent per-condition generation calls. The guarded arm permitted at most one repair call if the deterministic validator indicated a violation. The archived responses and provider traces record shared_initial_candidate content, shared_initial_response_path, and raw response SHA-256s for each task (representative examples included in artifact_examples). All raw model outputs, validator traces, repair traces (none applied), and analysis scripts are archived with hashes referenced in the execution manifest and analysis artifacts (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl sha256: e3af400a9167c27f2255003a02cf86f7b75381f96c64697014b55b77e753514b).

Statistical analysis. The preregistered primary test was the exact McNemar two-sided test for paired binary outcomes (α = 0.05) with a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI via 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor used was paired_binary_analysis_v1; artifact paths and CSV summaries are archived under analysis/*.csv with hashes in the manifest. Missingness and exclusion rules followed the preregistered complete_pair_primary policy; the run produced no exclusions (complete_pairs = 250).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and raw outcomes. The run started 2026-08-31T21:04:12Z and completed 2026-08-31T21:49:56Z (execution manifest). Planned episodes 500 (two conditions × 250 tasks) completed with failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 250; cache_miss_count = 250; stage_counts show a single shared_initial_generation stage executed 250 times (no independent per-condition sampling).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-backed). The archived paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; sha256: 1be58d8255423172b413b0f4908ac22bbf6527870fca0fd3dfa0d5908c987058) is: n11 = 250, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0; guarded VALID_CONFIGURATION rate = 250/250 = 1.0. Under actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION this yields zero actionable misconfigurations in both arms and a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv (hashes in manifest) record the same counts and no missingness.

Representative artifacts and repair traces. Validator traces for representative tasks (e.g., task-000004, task-000005, task-000006) show shared_initial_candidate content identical across baseline and guarded arms and record repair_applied = false for every guarded episode (artifact examples in execution/scoring/*.json files; representative hashes provided in the manifest). No repair_provider_trace entries exist because no repairs were invoked.

Preregistration deviation, reconciliation, and power mismatch. The preregistered conceptual plan targeted RAG poisoning tests at poison_fraction = 0.30; the executed adapter contract, however, set retrieval_augmented_generation = false and therefore did not perform retrievals or poison injections. Both the preregistration manifest and the execution manifest are archived: preregistration SHA (execution manifest field) = ebfbe67f56b5cfb4f0cdbf5a207c7cc095679771ab99515fa8d7d47b2f5e51e3; the execution/model_configuration.json artifact (sha256: a40e96e2...) explicitly records retrieval settings in the executed contract (retrieval_augmented_generation = false). The archived analysis_results metadata contains no post-execution deviations_from_preregistration entries (deviations_from_preregistration = []); this is because the execution followed the frozen adapter contract as archived (i.e., the run executed the recorded contract that disabled retrievals). In short: the original conceptual aim (test RAG poisoning) and the executed adapter contract diverged at execution design time; the run adhered to the archived executed contract (retrieval disabled). This reconciliation is documented in the execution manifest and model_configuration.json artifacts referenced above.

The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline actionable-misconfig rate ≈ 0.05 to detect an absolute paired increase ≈ 0.045–0.06 at N = 250. The observed baseline rate (0.0) violates that assumption and therefore the run does not have sensitivity to the originally preregistered RAG-poisoning effect sizes. We report this power/assumption mismatch explicitly and archive the artifacts (analysis_log.jsonl; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) supporting the conclusion.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation limited to the executed estimand. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the deterministic validator used (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), every sampled candidate already satisfied validator checks for the synthetic task bank: there was no opportunity for the guarded pipeline to change the paired outcome because no initial candidate violated the validator. The narrow, artifact-backed conclusion is therefore: when baseline and guarded arms start from the same sampled candidate that a deployed deterministic validator deems valid, the guarded pipeline (validator ± permitted single repair) cannot reduce actionable-misconfiguration counts and therefore yields zero paired difference.

What these results do not establish. These results do not imply guarded pipelines are unnecessary. The run did not exercise retrieval-augmented generation (no RAG), did not allow independent per-condition sampling, used a single LLM (declared gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator implemented as deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on synthetic tasks; it therefore cannot adjudicate the preregistered RAG-poisoning hypotheses nor generalize to production topologies, other models, or weaker validators. In particular, attacks that require poisoned retrieval contexts were not tested because retrievals were disabled in the executed contract.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: archived provider traces and deterministic_reconciliation.json confirm shared_initial_candidate semantics and one shared generation per task; this internal control isolates validator/repair effects but intentionally precludes detecting outcomes that require independent sampling variability. Construct validity: the deterministic validator enforces a specified rule set (reachability/policy constraints captured in validation traces) but may omit vendor-specific behavior, asynchronous device state, or hidden operational constraints. External validity: synthetic tasks, one model and one validator limit transferability to diverse real networks. Conclusion validity: homogeneous outcomes (all successes) yield exact CIs that reflect the controlled corpus rather than operational heterogeneity; the preregistered sensitivity assumptions therefore do not hold for this execution.

Operational implications and next-step preregistration. To test the original RAG-poisoning estimand requires enabling retrieval_augmented_generation, a controlled synthetic-poison corpus with provenance flags and containment checks, and independent per-condition generation (generation_semantics != shared_initial_candidate). Follow-up preregistrations should (a) declare retrieval settings and poison fractions, (b) reserve a discovery partition for defense tuning, (c) broaden validators to vendor-aware simulators, and (d) include multiple LLMs or sampling regimes. We preserve these points as concrete, artifact-grounded future targets rather than retrofitting the present run's evidence.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired experiment of a guarded generate→validate→repair NetOps pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics (declared model: gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; retrieval disabled). All 250 shared sampled candidates passed deterministic validation (n11 = 250), no repairs were applied, and the paired difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate is 0.0 (McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0]). Because retrieval augmentation was disabled in the executed contract, the preregistered RAG/poisoning hypotheses were not testable; we documented and reconciled this execution-time realization against the archived preregistration and execution artifacts. Follow-up preregistered runs that enable controlled retrieval augmentation, independent per-condition sampling, broader validators, and multi-model ensembles are necessary to measure guarded pipelines' mitigation potential under adversarial retrievals and sampling variability.

limitations: The executed design used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate with exactly one sampled initial generation per task reused across arms; it therefore measures validator/repair effects on the same candidate and cannot detect differences that require independent per-condition generation variability.

Retrieval-augmented generation was disabled in the executed adapter (retrieval_augmented_generation = false); the preregistered poisoning/RAG hypotheses and dose–response analyses were therefore not testable in this run and are recorded as an execution-time realization documented in the execution manifest and model_configuration.json artifact.

The stored scorer semantics required explicit mapping to the preregistered estimand: archived VALID_CONFIGURATION = 1 corresponds to no actionable misconfiguration, hence actionable_misconfig = 1 − VALID_CONFIGURATION. This mapping was applied consistently in all reported analyses.

A single declared LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were used on synthetic tasks; these choices limit external validity to diverse production topologies, vendor semantics, and multi-model ensembles.

The model configuration recorded temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling—hosted-model nondeterminism may remain and is logged in archived provider traces. The observed zero-event outcome (no actionable misconfigs) violates the preregistered baseline-rate assumption (≈0.05) and therefore does not constitute a sensitive test of the original poisoning hypothesis.
